instruction: Configure Thunderbird to forward all future emails from anonym-x2024@outlook.com to archive-2024@protonmail.com. Set this up locally in the Thunderbird client without modifying the online account.

metadata.explanation: Variation with different forward target email (archive-2024@protonmail.com). Evaluator verifies filter is enabled, action is Forward, target is archive-2024@protonmail.com, and condition is ALL. Same complexity as original.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic mismatch: Instruction requires forwarding emails FROM anonym-x2024@outlook.com, but evaluator only checks condition=['ALL'] which accepts ALL emails regardless of sender
Incomplete verification coverage: The evaluator does not verify the source email filter (from anonym-x2024@outlook.com) - only 75% of requirements are checked (3/4)
False positive risk: A user could create a filter that forwards ALL emails to archive-2024@protonmail.com (not just from anonym-x2024@outlook.com) and the evaluator would incorrectly pass
The expected.rules should include a condition check for the FROM field matching 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com', not just condition=['ALL']
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Update expected.rules.expect[0].condition to verify the filter includes a FROM condition. Based on the Thunderbird filter format (see check_thunderbird_filter at src/envs/osworld_env/desktop_env/evaluators/metrics/thunderbird.py:118-122), the condition field should contain a pattern like 'AND (from,is,anonym-x2024@outlook.com)' or similar
The expected structure should be: {'enabled': 'yes', 'action': 'Forward', 'actionValue': 'archive-2024@protonmail.com', 'condition': [pattern matching 'from' field with 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com']}
Verify that _match_record function can correctly match the condition field patterns - may need to adjust the matching logic or use a different comparison method for condition patterns
